sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Middle-Market Cross-Border Cross-Industry M&A Advisory Boutique

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified under the Taiwan Civil Code); commercial regulation influenced by German/Japanese precedent and U.S. financial/AML practice
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Economic Cooperation Framework Agreement (ECFA) signed 29 June 2010
Cross-Strait Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement signed 31 August 2012 under ECFA
Cross-Strait Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement signed 24 August 2015
Singapore-Taiwan Economic Partnership Agreement (ASTEP) signed 9 July 2013

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Taiwan Money Laundering Control Act (2018 consolidated version) Articles 5, 7, 8 and 12; Company Act Article 18 and Article 393; Financial Supervisory Commission 'Standards Governing Due Diligence and Continued Customer Support Measures for Certain Non-Financial Businesses' (2019); Ministry of Economic Affairs 'Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review Processing Regulations'; Cabinet-level AML/CFT regulations applicable to Corporate Service Providers and Trust Service Providers (Company Act amendment 2018). Beneficial ownership information must be collected for all legal persons, and company registrations are filed with the Department of Commercial Affairs.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certificate of incorporation and good standing for each non-Taiwan corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) of the People's Republic of China or the competent registry in the shareholder's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for jurisdictions acceded to 1961 Hague Convention; for Mainland China documents used in Taiwan, notarization by a PRC notary office followed by Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) cross-strait verification; supplementary consular legalization by the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office where the foreign authority requires it

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution of each corporate shareholder authorizing formation of the Sino-foreign equity joint venture
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized at source, apostilled/consular legalized as above, and filed with the Taiwan company registry as a corporate governance document

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Joint Venture Contract for CN_JV_LTD
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representatives of all JV parties, countersigned by Taiwan counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Signed before a PRC notary or Taiwan notary, then subjected to cross-strait formalities if executed in mainland China; no apostille is accepted as a substitute for cross-strait verification in Taiwan

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of UBO passport/identity card and proof of registered address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary office at the UBO's place of residence or foreign notary authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille (Hague) plus English/Chinese translation, or consular legalization via Taipei Economic and Cultural Office if awarding authority is not a Hague member; for Mainland UBOs, notarized at PRC notary and verified through SEF/ARATS

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: AML/CFT beneficial ownership declaration form (possibly with evidence of wealth/source of funds for enhanced due diligence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Proposed JV company, prepared by the licensed Taiwan corporate service provider
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Company internal record; notarization of signatures on the form is recommended and must be authenticated where the signatory is overseas

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of every director, UBO and authorized signatory against U.S. OFAC Specially Designated Nationals list, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, European Union consolidated financial sanctions list, Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission published AML/CFT sanctions, and PRC foreign-sanctions lists. PEP (domestic and foreign) status triggers enhanced due diligence including senior management approval, documented source of wealth/funds, and six-month transaction monitoring. For a M&A advisory boutique, any politically exposed person, sanctioned entity, or shell counterpart with opaque UBO structure must be refused unless a separate enhanced compliance plan is approved by the responsible person and reported to the competent authority when required.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs - Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Review System (公司名稱暨所營事業預查案件進度查詢) at https://gcis.nat.gov.tw
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be in traditional Chinese characters. English names are permitted for international branding but do not confer statutory corporate-name protection. Transliteration of a foreign corporate name must follow a standard Mandarin romanization scheme and may not create confusion with an existing registered company. Simplified Chinese characters are not accepted for the Chinese corporate name. The name must be distinctive and must reflect the licensed scope; for a Sino-Foreign JV, the name may not denote a foreign state or government unless specially approved.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the pre-approval application is rejected, the applicant may, within 30 days after service of the rejection, file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs under Article 1 and Article 14 of the Administrative Appeal Act. The appeal must annex the refusal notice, a revised Chinese name (if such revision cures the defect), and supporting evidence of non-conflicting name (e.g., trademark search or business-scope explanation). The Ministry of Economic Affairs must issue a decision within two months. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may initiate an administrative suit before the Taipei High Administrative Court within two months of the dismissal. Name pre-approval valid for 180 days is non-extendable; upon expiry the applicant must re-submit the pre-approval application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual mailbox without physical Taiwan office space is not permissible for a licensed M&A advisory enterprise. The Business Registration Act requires a fixed operational premises capable of receiving government and judicial service. A registered virtual office is tolerated only if backed by an actual desk/meeting-space lease and a management-service agreement in Taiwan; the name plaque and records must be accessible during business hours. Remote working arrangements do not displace the registered office requirement.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 25% to 35% probability of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months for a cross-border M&A boutique requiring a business license; the risk rises to approximately 50% if the entity uses an external virtual office provider without an on-site employee, or if a PEP/foreign responsible person is appointed.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name and business scope pre-approval application fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commercial Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee NT$300 per application under the Company Registration Regulations and business scope pre-review tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs / municipal tax authority

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Authentication and cross-strait legalization of the incorporation bundle (articles, good standing, board resolution, UBO IDs)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: PRC notary office, Straits Exchange Foundation, Taiwan overseas representative office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff and SEF verification fee; apostille fees abroad where applicable; actual third-party courier excluded

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/OFAC/UN/PRC/Taiwan sanction screening and AML/CFT compliance file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Taiwan AML/CFT compliance service provider or CPA firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 225-325 for medium-risk M&A advisory client file preparation, including PEP assessment and source of funds review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal opinion and joint venture incorporation support (Sino-Foreign JV eligibility, FIP approval if applicable, share structure, corporate governance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing Taipei market fixed fee for a straightforward JV incorporation under Company Act and Foreign Investment Act, excluding complex PIT regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and first-year corporate secretary/registered agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed Taiwan registered agent / corporate service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Annual market benchmark for a fixed site, registered address obligation, and handling of government correspondence for a professional-services company

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Translation, notarization and courier of Chinese-language corporate documents (if executed in Simplified Chinese or English)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Actual or prevailing fixed translation tariff (USD 35-45 per document) plus secure courier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Company seal carver, municipal labor and finance bureaus
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Non-statutory market rate for seal engraving and minor filing fees; no central tariff applies for seals

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Republic of China (Taiwan) Companies Act (公司法), Articles 98, 128-129, 154, 156, 171-172, 192, 208; Act for Relations between the Peoples of the Taiwan Area and the Mainland Area (兩岸人民關係條例); Regulations Governing Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area People (大陸地區人民來臺投資許可辦法); Money Laundering Control Act (洗錢防制法), Article 5; Securities and Exchange Act (證券交易法), Articles 18 and 18-1.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部商業發展署) — Company Registration Division; post-registration tax and labor filings with the National Taxation Bureau, the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Registration Application (公司設立登記申請書) and the Certificate of Company Registration (公司登記證明書), together with the Investment Commission approval letter and the name pre-approval certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for a general company limited by shares; for a mainland-area joint-venture investor, the approved paid-in capital must be remitted into the company's pre-establishment (preparation office) bank account only after Investment Commission permission and must be verified by a licensed CPA before registration. No mandatory escrow; the funds remain frozen in the preparation account until the CPA capital verification report is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, unanimously, by the Board of Directors at the inaugural meeting held at the registered office on [DATE]: 1. The executed Articles of Incorporation and the subscription list appended thereto are adopted and ratified, and the paid-in capital comprising [●] ordinary shares is approved as fully subscribed. 2. The registered head office of the Company is fixed and approved at [ADDRESS], Taiwan (R.O.C.). 3. [●] and [●] are appointed as Directors, [●] as Supervisor, and [●] is elected Chairman of the Board. 4. [●] is appointed General Manager and [●] is appointed Compliance and AML Officer, jointly authorized to execute all incorporation, investment-approval, licensing and banking filings and to appoint signatories. All resolutions passed unanimously; meeting adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the Company Name and Business Scope (Name Pre-Approval)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce — One-Stop Integrated Business Registration Portal (https://onestop.nat.gov.tw)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the MOEA One-Stop Portal and file the Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval application for a company limited by shares (股份有限公司). Submit up to five ranked Chinese and English name candidates, declare the main business scope as management consulting services (管理顧問業, ISIC 7020) and general investment advisory services (一般投資顧問業), and pay the NT$300 name-check fee. Download the pre-approval certificate, which is valid for six months and is a prerequisite for subsequent Investment Commission and registration filings.
required_dossiers: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Approval application form
Up to five Chinese/English name candidates
Proposed business scope items
Power of attorney appointing the local incorporated agent/representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, re-file immediately with revised candidates; if a business scope item is deemed regulated, delete the regulated item and apply to the Financial Supervisory Commission separately for the specific investment-consulting licence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Mainland-Area Investment Permission for the Joint-Venture Shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部投資審議委員會)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an online application under the Regulations Governing Investment in Taiwan by Mainland Area People. Provide the joint-venture agreement, shareholding ratio, capital and remittance plan, draft Articles of Incorporation and the business plan. The Investment Commission will examine the investment's economic benefit, national security and employment impact, and issue a conditional approval letter. Remittance of capital is permitted only after this approval is granted.
required_dossiers: Standard investment application form
Joint-venture agreement executed between mainland and Taiwan shareholders
Business plan with capital and financing table
Draft Articles of Incorporation
Notarized identification and qualification documents of the mainland investor
Power of attorney for the Taiwan agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On deficiency notification, supplementary documents must be filed within the statutory cure period (typically 45 days); if the investment is rejected, the joint venture may be restructured by lowering the mainland shareholding or replacing the investor, and the application may be re-submitted for a fresh review or administratively appealed to the Executive Yuan.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute Articles of Incorporation, Share Subscriptions and Inaugural Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private corporate act effected by the founding shareholders and authenticated by the company's legal counsel; documents signed outside Taiwan must be legalized by the Taipei Representative Office in the home jurisdiction.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All subscribers execute the Articles of Incorporation and the share subscription list, elect at least one director and one supervisor (two directors proposed for the JV), hold the inaugural board meeting, adopt the first board resolution, and have the minutes signed by the convener. Authenticate the signature of the mainland shareholder at a notary in the home jurisdiction and, if required, legalize at the Taiwan representative office to ensure bank and registry acceptance.
required_dossiers: Articles of Incorporation executed by all subscribers
Share subscription list with amounts paid and unpaid
Minutes of the incorporation/inaugural board meeting and the first board resolution
Consent-to-act forms of directors and supervisors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry or the Investment Commission queries the minutes or the electoral procedure, convene a supplementary meeting, pass a curative resolution and file amended minutes; a disqualified director must be replaced by a new election before the registration deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Preparation-Office Bank Account, Remit Paid-In Capital and Obtain CPA Capital Verification Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated foreign-exchange bank (authorized banking institution under the Central Bank of China, Taiwan) and a licensed certified public accountant (會計師).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the Investment Commission approval letter, the name pre-approval certificate and the Articles, open a preparation-office bank account in the exact proposed company name. Remit the approved paid-in capital via SWIFT from the mainland investor; obtain the bank deposit certificate and the foreign-exchange inward-remittance certificate. Instruct a licensed CPA to verify the capital and issue the Capital Verification Report (資本額查核報告書) and a declaration that no shares have been issued at a discount and the capital is fully paid in cash.
required_dossiers: Investment Commission approval letter
Bank deposit certificate issued by the preparation-office account bank
Foreign-exchange inward remittance certificate
CPA capital verification report
Articles of Incorporation and name pre-approval certificate
Board resolution authorizing bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the remittance is queried for foreign-exchange compliance, the remitter must correct beneficiary details and re-remit; if the bank refuses the account opening, select another designated bank and re-submit the same corporate dossier; the capital verification report is reissued only after the full capital is actually collected.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (財政部), administered regionally by the National Taxation Bureau (各地區國稅局) with jurisdiction over the JV's registered office; official e-portal: Ministry of Finance e-Tax Online Services (電子稅務入口網, https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw); e-filing for Business Tax via the Business Tax E-Notice/E-Declaration system (營業稅電子申報繳稅系統); Unified Business Number (統一編號) issued through the Ministry of Economic Affairs company registry (https://www.moea.gov.tw).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Obtain MOEA investment approval (Investment Commission) for the mainland-China JV shareholder and incorporate the limited company under the Company Act; the 8-digit Unified Business Number is assigned on the company registration certificate and serves as the tax ID. 2. Within 15 days of incorporation or before commencing business, file the Business Tax Registration Application (營業登記申請書) with the local National Taxation Bureau, attaching the certificate of incorporation, articles, registered-office proof, domestic agent appointment for the foreign shareholder, and bank account details. 3. Open a foreign-currency deposit account and obtain exchange-settlement authorization from an authorized domestic bank. 4. Enroll in the E-Invoice Integrated Service Platform (電子發票整合服務平台) and elect a Turnkey API or value-added center transmission mode. 5. Complete employer registration for payroll withholding; Uniform Invoice (統一發票) registration is consolidated into the same tax registration file.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — CN_JV_LTD, being incorporated in Taiwan, is a resident profit-seeking enterprise taxed on worldwide income at 20% CIT (Income Tax Act Art. 3), plus a 5% undistributed-retained-earnings surtax under Art. 66-9 where profits are not distributed; the integrated imputation credit system applies to resident shareholders. Non-resident shareholders are subject to statutory dividend withholding at 21% (or the applicable non-resident rate; no comprehensive income tax treaty is in force, including for the mainland-China shareholder). No pass-through or partnership classification is available by election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No U.S.-style check-the-box election exists; entity classification follows the legal form. Relevant elections for an M&A boutique: (i) affiliated-group consolidated return election under Income Tax Act Art. 39-1 (parent holding ≥90% of the subsidiary); (ii) tax-deferred reorganization and loss-carries election under the Business Mergers and Acquisitions Act; (iii) functional-currency election for bookkeeping with NT$ tax translation; (iv) advance pricing agreement or individual letter ruling application for hybrid instrument transfer-pricing; (v) foreign income tax credit election for offshore-source success fees. Hybrid-mismatch and CFC/PEM provisions (Income Tax Act Art. 43-3/43-4) are mandatory anti-avoidance rules, not elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax (加值型及非加值型營業稅法) — destination-based VAT with a single business tax filing; professional and consulting services are taxable at the general rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration before commencing business (Business Tax Act Art. 28); no threshold applies to a corporation. Small-scale operators with average monthly turnover below NT$80,000 (≈US$2,500) may apply for exemption from registration; monthly turnover of NT$80,000–NT$200,000 is taxed at a special 1% rate (Art. 13); the standard 5% rate applies above NT$200,000 and to all professional service firms.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic Uniform Invoices (電子統一發票) are mandatory for all registered operators. Invoices must be transmitted to the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integrated Service Platform (財政部電子發票整合服務平台) within 48 hours of issuance via the Turnkey (加值中心) integration API or a certified value-added service center; the platform performs cross-matching of invoice serial numbers, customs declarations and foreign-currency receipt data. Each e-invoice carries an 8-digit serial number plus a 2-digit random authentication code (digital stamp); B2B/B2C clearance is near-real-time, and zero-rated export invoices are flagged for refund audit.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Business Tax Act Art. 7(3), export of advisory services qualifies for 0% VAT where (a) the services are rendered to a foreign enterprise without a fixed place of business in Taiwan (or are performed abroad), (b) the deliverable is actually used outside Taiwan, and (c) the consideration is received in foreign currency. Success fees, retainers and due-diligence fees charged by the M&A boutique to non-Taiwan clients (e.g., mainland-China parent or offshore acquisition vehicles), with the engagement report used abroad, are zero-rated; input VAT on local costs becomes refundable. Services used in Taiwan or rendered to a Taiwan branch of a foreign company are taxable at 5%. Foreign-currency receipt must be effected within 180 days (extendable to 270 days with the handling bank's approval or 365 days with Central Bank consent).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口報單) for any physical deliverables; replaced by a Service Export Statement for pure advisory engagements.
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (提單) for tangible closing books, data-room exhibits or transaction materials physically shipped.
Inward Remittance Certificate (外匯收入水單/匯入匯款通知書) or bank exchange-settlement record evidencing collection of fees in foreign currency.
Original signed advisory/engagement agreement specifying cross-border scope, place of use of the deliverable, and fee currency.
Zero-rated Uniform Invoice (零稅率統一發票) annotated with the Art. 7 zero-rating code and the foreign client's particulars.
Proof of the foreign client's non-resident status (certificate of incorporation or business registration).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated export claims are a priority audit target: the National Taxation Bureau automatically cross-checks e-invoice data against customs records and foreign-exchange receipts. Where substantiation fails (e.g., no foreign-currency collection, services used in Taiwan, fabricated offshore clients), the supply is retroactively reclassified as 5% taxable: underpaid VAT plus interest is collected, and a penalty of 5 to 10 times the underpaid tax is imposed (Business Tax Act Art. 51; Tax Collection Act Art. 44). Forged contracts or backdated remittances trigger criminal liability under Tax Collection Act Art. 41 (up to 5 years' imprisonment and a fine of up to NT$5,000,000); the assessment period extends from 5 to 7 years for fraudulent evasion, and customs smuggling liability may attach where goods are involved.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) — State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CNY is fully convertible for current-account transactions (trade in services including M&A advisory success fees) under SAFE's verification-based regime, but strictly controlled on the capital account. Profit remittance and dividends by a Sino-foreign equity joint venture require annual audit, tax clearance, board resolution on profit distribution, and bank verification under SAFE Circular 16/2019. Equity capital injection, shareholder loans, and repayment of overseas borrowings require prior SAFE registration (FDI registration or Foreign Debt registration). There is no free convertibility for speculative or non-trade capital flows; cross-border M&A advisory fees from non-resident clients are treated as service trade revenue and enjoy current-account convertibility once authentic commercial documents, invoices, contracts, and proof of service completion are submitted to the designated bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current SAFE rules, export proceeds from cross-border services rendered by the M&A boutique must be repatriated to a licensed bank in China. Mandatory forced conversion was abolished in 2012; therefore enterprises may retain 100% of qualified export/service proceeds in domestic foreign-currency accounts or voluntarily convert into RMB at market rates. The enterprise must go through 'repatriation and verification' within 30 days after the contractual payment due date or receipt, at the bank where the service trade receipt is booked, presenting the service contract, commercial invoice, proof of service performance, and a SAFE service-trade payment/receipt application. Failure to repatriate within the statutory period triggers SAFE penalty and removal from the 'A-level enterprise' convenience regime. The same rules apply to success fees charged to overseas targets or acquirers in cross-border M&A engagements, with no differentiated conversion ratio.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI Foreign Currency Capital Account / RMB Capital Account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Current Account (Basic RMB Account and FCY Settlement Account)
Operational Current Account plus sub-accounts for Success-Fee Wire Settlement
Dual-currency Operational Account / Escrow-qualified Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium, with significant legal constraints. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Airwallex, Currenxie, and neobank-style Payment and Electronic Money Institutions regulated in Hong Kong, Singapore, or the UK) are viable for collecting or disbursing small-ticket cross-border success-fee wires from foreign clients or paying transaction bonus milestones to overseas counterparties, but they cannot lawfully open the mandatory RMB Basic Deposit Account inside mainland China. Under PBOC licensing rules, such EMIs lack a deposit-taking banking license and cannot hold client funds as bank deposits; they operate as payment facilitators or foreign-exchange agents. For the M&A advisory boutique, an offshore EMI account may be used as an ancillary collections rail for non-China counterparties, but full treasury control requires a licensed onshore domestic bank relationship; custody of deal escrow funds, regulatory-significant subscription payments, or SAFE-monitored capital flows must remain in a tier-1 commercial bank. Legal caution: China's cybersecurity, data-residency, and cross-border data transfer rules limit the use of fully offshore financial dashboards and user interfaces by a JV whose servers or records sit within PRC territory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For capital-account-related account opening (e.g., FDI Capital Escrow Account), the legal representative, a non-resident director with full signatory power, or the authorized finance manager must appear in person at a mainland China bank branch. Most tier-1 banks require a physical board-meeting presence or, at minimum, an in-person notarized/legalized power of attorney when the JV's legal representative is based outside mainland China. Remote video-based KYC interviews are offered only for low-risk current-account settlement accounts in selected Free Trade Zone pilot branches, and only after the underlying entity is fully registered with SAFE and has provided stamped corporate documents. For capital escrow accounts, in-person verification of the original unified social credit code certificate, the JV approval certificate or filed foreign-investment information report, and the SAFE FDI registration form is mandatory. The Taiwan-resident director or beneficial owner will normally be required to travel to Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, or another designated branch with original identity documents and proof of personal source of funds; apostille/legalization of Taiwan-issued corporate documents is required through the mainland/Taiwan notarization liaison system.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership chain includes opaque offshore holding vehicles or nominee shareholder arrangements, triggering the bank's 'higher-risk customer' classification under Article 9 of the Anti-Money Laundering Law (2020 revision).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full shareholding chart on a notarized statutory declaration; AIFC/organization charts across each layer; original certificate of incorporation and good standing; audited financial statements of each intermediate holding company; sworn affidavit from the Taiwan ultimate beneficial owner disclosing source of initial capital; legal opinion from a PRC-licensed attorney confirming the chain has no undisclosed beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection sourced from an unrelated third party or from a jurisdiction on the FATF/I-CRG list, raising concern under SAFE's authenticity-and-compliance rule for FDI capital remittances.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Chinese- and English-language equity subscription agreement; board resolution approving the capital call; bank statement showing funding originates directly from the registered shareholder's account; shareholder's corporate annual report or paid-in capital ledger; sworn indemnity covenant; structured finance source documentation; and a pre-filed SAFE FDI registration page listing the exact amount, date, and affiliate routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Success-fee wire exhibits unusual invoicing timing: fee invoiced before the closing of a merger, causing the bank to suspect trade-based money laundering or a disguised dividend distribution.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dated engagement letter with clearly defined success-fee trigger and calculation formula; closing memorandum and transaction stamp; client-side confirmation of deal closing; itemized bank account ledger showing receipt of the closing payment by the counterparty; final invoice bilingual set; independent legal counsel's closing certificate; SOW and work-product log evidencing actual M&A advisory service milestones.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Taiwan-registered shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner appears on sanctions/PEP screening lists, triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Professional KYC screening report from an internationally recognized database; residence and business-activity certificate from the competent authority in Taiwan; criminal-record certificate; negative media search; proof that the JV has no actual or apparent nexus to prohibited persons; SAFE's whistleblower/no-sanctions declaration; corporate governance policy against sanctions evasion; and external sanctions-compliance opinion issued by a law firm.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing begins with the Shanghai/Shenzhen/Beijing local SAFE office registration of the Sino-foreign equity joint venture's FDI quota and capital account. The Taiwan shareholder or its designated offshore entity then wires the agreed equity injection through SWIFT MT103 from its own bank account to the JV's designated Capital Escrow Account at the Chinese tier-1 bank. SAFE reconciliation requires the remitter name and account number to match the registered shareholder; the payment purpose message must be tagged with SAFE purpose code 'JINJIN' / 'FDI Equity Injection' and quote the valid FDI registration certificate number, if required by the receiving bank. The bank will verify the source-of-funds evidence, board resolution, the original executed joint venture contract (with notarization), and the unified social credit code certificate before crediting the account. Any capital payment in kind (e.g., technology or equipment) must be declared to customs and appraised; cash wiring is accepted for monetary subscription only. If the capital amount exceeds the registered FDI quota, a separate SAFE capital-account adjustment application is mandatory before remittance; otherwise, the surplus will be rejected or suspended for anti-money-laundering review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For distribution of M&A transaction-related success fees, monthly retainers, or reimbursement of overseas professional expenses from the JV's operation account: SWIFT MT103 is the primary clearing rail, sent through the JV's domestic bank to the beneficiary's account in Taiwan or any other jurisdiction. For cross-border RMB settlement, the bank uses the CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) rail with the MT103 message mapped to the e-CIP standard; the payment purpose must be classified as 'service trade remuneration' or 'M&A advisory fee' under the correct SAFE purpose code. Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700) are permissible only when the payment is embedded in a documentary transaction, e.g., where a cross-border acquisition agreement requires the escrow of fees through an L/C guarantee; a pure advisory success fee normally cannot be routed through an L/C without an underlying physical trade document, thus commercial L/Cs are assessed as Low usability for this boutique. For outbound disbursements to INR, JPY, USD, or EUR, the domestic bank applies the daily FX rate and debits the corresponding RMB balance; no separate foreign-currency account is required. For urgent settlement of a cross-border closing fee to a target-company counsel in a time-zone-sensitive transaction, SWIFT MT103 with 'Priority: Urgent' and detailed remittance information is the recommended rail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CNY/USD, CNY/EUR, or CNY/JPY outright forwards with genuine current-account or capital-account underlying exposure, subject to the bank's real-demand background verification under SAFE Circular 35/2013.
CNY/CNH Cross-Currency Forwards executed between the JV, its onshore bank, and an offshore affiliate or clearing bank for economic hedging of transaction fees payable in CNH or foreign currency.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in USD/CNH, executed offshore or through an onshore bank with an offshore NDF booking branch, permissible for hedging expected success-fee inflows denominated in USD from Taiwan or other non-PRC counterparties, while prudently avoiding speculative positions outside the safety of the real-business-boundary rule.

Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS) between RMB and USD/EUR for tenor-matched assets and liabilities arising from cross-border M&A holdback escrow conditions; permitted when the contract generates scheduled principal and interest payments.

Plain-vanilla FX options (European calls/puts) used exclusively for hedges backed by executed M&A transaction agreements; banks require the JV to provide the signed engagement letter, expected fee schedule, and underlying client-mandate documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau of Taiwan (Ministry of Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 1% monthly surcharge on unpaid tax (max 15%), plus a delinquency fee of 3% per month; persistent delinquency triggers tax lien and administrative enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audited/Reviewed Financial Statements after Shareholders' Approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Department of Commercial Affairs, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: June 30 (within 6 months after fiscal year end and after AGM approval)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of NT$10,000–NT$50,000 and an order to rectify within a prescribed period; continued default may result in administrative strike-off of registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) – Company Registration Online System

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of NT$50,000–NT$500,000 for non-filing or false declaration; daily accruing penalty for non-rectification; potential judicial cancellation by court order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Operation Report (for foreign-invested JV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 (within 3 months after fiscal year end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of NT$30,000–NT$150,000 for late or missing filing; suspension of foreign exchange remittance privileges and future investment applications until compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: CPA-audited financial statements are compulsory where paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million, annual revenue exceeds NT$30 million, or headcount exceeds 100 persons. Below these thresholds, financial statements may be internally reviewed unless the JV charter or Investment Commission approval mandates certification. Given the boutique's transaction flow, audit is typically required by the MOEAIC license conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (T-IFRS) for financial years starting after 2015; small and medium-sized entities may apply T-IFRS for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: All shareholding transfers must be reflected in the UBO register within 30 days of the change. Annually, the company must file with MOEA a confirmation statement of current ultimate beneficial owners by March 31. The statement must list natural persons with 25% or more control via shares, votes, or other means. Failure to re-confirm results in administrative fines and automatic suspension of corporate acts.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,500 – USD 20,000 per year (basis: transaction volume and CPA firm tier)
